title: Digital arrest
persona: Mrs. Sunita Rao, 68, retired teacher, Bengaluru
blurb: A "Mumbai Crime Branch officer" says a parcel with drugs was sent in her name. Within minutes she is on a video call with a "CBI DCP" and being told to move ₹48 lakh to an "RBI verification account".

title: Bank card OTP
blurb: "SBI card protection" calls about a ₹49,999 transaction he never made. To "cancel" it he must read out his card number, CVV and the OTP.

title: Courier parcel hand-off
blurb: A FedEx IVR, a "compliance executive", then a conference call with a "cyber-crime inspector": the classic on-ramp to a digital arrest.

title: Investment WhatsApp group
blurb: A "SEBI-registered analyst" with screenshots of members' profits, an app that shows gains, and a withdrawal that needs a "tax" first.

title: Grandparent voice clone
blurb: "Grandma, it's me, I've been in an accident, don't tell Mom." A cloned voice, then a "lawyer" who needs bail money in cash.

title: Tech support remote access
blurb: "Microsoft" says his computer is sending error messages. He installs AnyDesk; next, his bank app is on the scammer's screen.

title: Deepfake CFO wire request
blurb: The "CFO" joins a video call about a confidential acquisition and needs three wires today, no loop-in, no callback.

title: Genuine bank fraud call
blurb: HDFC's real fraud team blocks a card the right way: no OTP, no urgency, and an invitation to call back on the number on the card.

title: Genuine hospital call
blurb: Apollo confirms an appointment, asks her to bring reports, and says payment happens at the counter after the visit.
